title: API tokens can mint additional API tokens
reasoning: POST /auth/tokens only depends on get_current_user, and get_current_user treats a valid gw_ API token as a user credential. That lets any existing API token create another persistent API token for the same user. If a device token is compromised, an attacker can create a sibling token before revocation, so revoking the originally exposed token does not actually remove access.
reproduction: Create an API token with a JWT, then call POST /api/auth/tokens again using that token in X-API-Key or Authorization: Bearer. The handler will create and return a second token.
recommendation: Require an interactive JWT/session credential for token-management routes, or have get_current_user return authentication context and reject API-token-authenticated requests in create_api_token.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover POST /auth/tokens, and the existing token tests only create tokens directly or use JWT auth for plugin download.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a route test that POST /api/auth/tokens succeeds with a JWT but returns 401/403 when authenticated with an existing gw_ API token.
minimumFixScope: Update authentication context or this route's dependency so token creation rejects API-token credentials, then add route-level coverage for JWT success and API-token rejection.
